transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-10-05 16:00 UTC · 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Lena (Aurora CTO), Ravi (Aurora Head Security), Emily (Infra), Samir (Compliance)

Summary: quick security walkthrough focused on encryption and key mgmt, some deep dive Qs on HSM and BYOK, talked about audit logs and SOC2 artifacts.

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll run through our encryption posture and the BYOK/HSM story, Diego will jump into the tech details
00:12 - Lena: thanks, quick note we have strict PCI and local data residency needs, so this is high priority
00:20 - Diego: cool, so high level Redwood encrypts data in transit with TLS 1.2/1.3 and at rest using AES-256-GCM, keys are managed via cloud KMS or customer-provided keys (BYOK).
00:38 - Ravi: when you say BYOK, do you support HSM-backed keys? we can't have pure software keys in our control plane
00:45 - Diego: yes, we support HSM-backed key material, you can bring keys from CloudHSM or external HSM via import or have keys stored in your KMS (AWS KMS with custom key store, GCP CMEK with HSM SLA)
01:05 - Jordan: slight caveat, for Hosted mode we isolate key material at rest but the control plane needs to orchestrate. For Private and Dedicated you can configure a customer-managed KMS endpoint and we never see plaintext keys.
01:27 - Emily: can you confirm key usage model? are data encryption keys ephemeral and wrapped?
01:33 - Diego: yes, we use envelope encryption. Root/master keys live in the KMS/HSM, we generate DEKs (data encryption keys) per-tenant which are wrapped with the KMS key. DEKs are rotated and versioned, and cached in memory on nodes but never persisted unwrapped.
01:55 - Ravi: what's the rotation cadence and is it automatic? we need proof of rotation for audits
02:02 - Jordan: rotation can be scheduled; for BYOK you can rotate keys in your KMS and Redwood will pick up new key versions via the configured key ARN. We log version changes in audit logs; we can provide rotation reports for SOC2/PCI evidence.
02:25 - Samir: audit logs — are they tamper-evident and how long do you retain?
02:30 - Maya: by default hosted logs retained 90 days, Dedicated/Private configurable; we can export to your SIEM (S3, GCS, Splunk) and support WORM-like retention on request. Logs include key usage events, API calls, and key version operations.
02:50 - Lena: network topology — if we go Private, do you deploy inside our VPC? we need traffic to stay internal
02:56 - Diego: yes, Private deploys run in your VPC, all control plane connections can be restricted, and we support private endpoints and peering, so data never traverses public internet.
03:15 - Emily: curious about HSM import and cryptographic boundaries — can we import keys generated on our on-prem HSM into cloud KMS or do you recommend Cloud HSM?
03:25 - Diego: you have two patterns: 1) generate keys in your HSM and keep them there, use external signing and key unwrap operations via API (Redwood calls your KMS through private link). 2) import key material into a customer-managed KMS (some clouds allow key import with wrapped blobs), but note not all HSMs allow export. We usually recommend keeping master keys in an HSM and performing wrap/unwrap in your KMS or HSM; Redwood integrates with both approaches.
03:58 - Ravi: encryption at rest for cached content and model artifacts? are KV caches encrypted and how do you manage ephemeral token caches?
04:06 - Jordan: KV cache in-memory is ephemeral and encrypted in transit between nodes. On-disk caches and model artifacts are encrypted with DEKs and those DEKs are wrapped by KMS. For Dedicated nodes we ensure disk encryption and for Private you can layer your own disk encryption keys (via CMEK).
04:32 - Maya: there may be some noisy language in the transcript, please ignore small transcription errors
04:36 - Lena: ok, regarding compliance, do you have FIPS validated crypto and attestation?
04:42 - Diego: our HSM integrations can be configured to use FIPS 140-2 validated modules depending on provider (AWS CloudHSM uses FIPS modules), we can provide attestation docs and CA cert chains where required.
05:02 - Samir: where do you store encryption keys for embeddings and prompts? we must ensure no PCI data is retained in model inputs or logs
05:15 - Jordan: model inputs are redacted by default in hosted mode with PII filters on request; we also recommend tokenization and local preprocessing. For keys, anything sensitive is encrypted with DEKs and only wrapped keys stored in metadata, not plaintext. We can disable logging of prompts for regulated customers.
05:40 - Ravi: how about BYOK lifecycle — if we revoke a key, how do you handle existing encrypted data?
05:46 - Diego: revoking a master key in the KMS will prevent unwrapping of DEKs that are wrapped with that key; we provide migration tools to rewrap DEKs with a new KMS key and we can run a re-encryption job. This is an important part of our POC checklist.
06:10 - Emily: does Redwood support external key signing operations where the private key never leaves our HSM (i.e., Redwood sends hash to our HSM for sign)?
06:18 - Jordan: yes that's supported in Private and Dedicated patterns via a proxy call to your KMS/HSM over private network; we do not require keys to be exported.
06:30 - Lena: can we get a short architecture diagram showing flow of wrapped keys, DEKs, and HSM boundary?
06:35 - Maya: yes we'll send the kms-byok-architecture.pdf and the integration doc.
06:40 - Ravi: audit log format — do you provide JSON structured logs with key IDs and request IDs?
06:46 - Diego: yes logs are structured JSON, include timestamp, actor, key_id, operation, source IP, request_id. We also support forwarding to your SIEM with HMAC-signed delivery for tamper evidence.
07:05 - Samir: for forensic timelines we need immutable audit trails; can you support append-only logs with retention policies?
07:12 - Maya: yes, for Dedicated/Private we can enable append-only logging and export to an S3 bucket with object lock enabled, or to your on-prem SIEM.
07:30 - Emily: encryption in transit between Redwood edges and model workers, is that mutual TLS?
07:36 - Jordan: mutual TLS is used internally for node-to-node. External API calls use TLS 1.2/1.3 with modern ciphers; we can configure mTLS for private peering.
07:50 - Lena: SLA questions — if there's a key availability outage in your KMS, do you have fallback keys or do calls fail closed? we need availability guarantees
07:58 - Diego: our policy is fail-closed for cryptographic operations: if KMS unwrapping fails we won't return plaintext. For high-availability we recommend using multi-region KMS or replicated keys in your KMS provider and configuring Redwood with multiple endpoints. For Dedicated we can co-locate an HSM-based key gateway in your region.
08:25 - Ravi: do you support hardware-backed key sealing for model weights or is that overkill?
08:31 - Jordan: we do support sealing model artifacts with keys stored in HSM if requested — that's common for regulated workloads.
08:40 - Maya: quick poll, has Aurora run an internal KMS proof-of-concept before?
08:45 - Emily: we run AWS KMS and use CloudHSM for some signing, but not for full BYOK for 3rd-party services yet
08:52 - Lena: timeline — we need production ready by Q1 2027, pilot earlier
08:58 - Maya: sounds reasonable; we'll map a POC plan in the next steps
09:05 - Ravi: licensing and contractual terms — do you have clauses for key escrow and support for subpoenas?
09:12 - Maya: we provide standard enterprise contract language; for BYOK where keys remain under customer control Redwood does not have access. For legal requests we would follow contractual obligations and notify customers, but specifics can be negotiated.
09:35 - Samir: can you share your SOC2 Type II report and ISO certs?
09:40 - Maya: yes will share links to SOC2 and ISO and also provide pen-test summaries, we will redact sensitive findings but provide scope and remediation notes.
09:55 - Jordan: some technical notes — we recommend using separate KMS keys per environment and per-tenant keys for stronger isolation; also use envelope encryption for large blobs to reduce KMS calls.
10:15 - Emily: are there rate limits on key operations? we have bursty traffic during settlement windows
10:22 - Diego: KMS providers do have API rate limits; we recommend DEK caching and batching unwrap operations to minimize calls. Redwood's runtime has a key cache with TTL and we can tune TTL for your bursts.
10:42 - Lena: what about key compromise detection and GC — do you maintain key usage analytics?
10:48 - Maya: yes analytics are in Redwood Console; we surface anomalous key usage and unusual unwrap patterns and can push alerts to PagerDuty or Slack.
11:05 - Ravi: HSM attestation — can we periodically request attestation from your environment?
11:12 - Diego: for customers using Redwood-managed HSMs we can provide attestation reports, but for Private/HSM-in-customer we direct you to your provider's attestation. We can also capture and forward attestation artifacts as part of onboarding.
11:30 - Jordan: small note, sometimes transcripts swap 'KMS' with 'kms' but the underlying config is case-insensitive, sorry for the noise
11:36 - Emily: what about data residency — we need all payments data to remain in eu-west-1, is that doable?
11:42 - Maya: yes Private or Dedicated in-region deployments ensure data stays in that region; Hosted can be region pinned for enterprise customers. We'll include a data residency addendum.
12:00 - Lena: ok let's recap next steps and owners
12:05 - Maya: recap: Maya send SOC2, KMS architecture diagram, security-deck.pdf; Diego prepare BYOK POC checklist and re-encryption plan; Emily provide network diagram and compliance requirements; schedule SE deep dive for BYOK testing.
12:28 - Lena: thanks all, that's it from us
12:31 - Maya: thanks everyone we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs

References mentioned: security-deck.pdf, kms-byok-architecture.pdf, kms-byok-integration.md, benchmark-sheet.xlsx
